about: siglia-saas-metrics reference, 26 Sep 2026 (1.4). Built from Research's deep-tier note on SaaS and AI metrics (F1-F8, rules 1-8), Research's rubric rulings of 26 Sep (rows B4, T3, X2 and X7, whose corrections govern, and the capex ruling. The held set is a 25-issuer snapshot of 16 Sep 2026 with about one SaaS name, measured by Corpus; its counts describe those names only. Register rows SE-46 to SE-49 and QF-49 are proposed in the research note and are not in the register yet. FASB ASC text is cited by reference and never quoted. A source item is a named file (label, then a file name, with an optional row or pack key: 'Corpus pack (file.json, KEY)'; its `anchors` must be in it), a fin-concepts register row ('siglia-fin-concepts SE-36', anchors in that row), a 17 CFR section (resolved in the cached eCFR: the section, its paragraph labels, the rule's single-quoted strings and its `absent` phrases), a FASB ASU cited by reference ('FASB ASU 2016-20 (..., sha256 HEX...)': never read or quoted here, no anchors; a named file the same row cites must hold its number and hash), or FASB taxonomy years (resolved offline: an element row's label, period and per-year `asc` references, with legacy references marked, every year's label compared by some item; `anchors` name elements that exist, `!` absent ones, `X ASC p` a reference, `X: words` documentation, `search WORDS = X, Y` a label search's whole result); items are separated by ' | '. An `asc` is one string for every year or one per year: paragraphs, each with an optional (S-X...), (legacy) or (common practice).

metrics.name: capitalized commissions (contract costs, ASC 340-40)
metrics.means: Incremental costs of obtaining a contract with a customer, such as a sales commission, are capitalized as an asset when the company expects to recover them (ASC 340-40-25-1, 25-2, by reference): the test is recoverability, not contract length. They may be expensed as incurred when the asset's amortization period would be one year or less (25-4, a practical expedient). The asset is amortized as the related goods or services transfer, over a period that may include specific anticipated contracts such as renewals (35-1). So a SaaS company's sales and marketing expense can lag its commission cash. The us-gaap elements are wider than commissions: they hold every capitalized cost to obtain or to fulfill a contract with a customer.
metrics.source: Research checks 2026-09-26-b2-skill-checks.md `The test is recoverability, not contract length. Incremental costs of obtaining a contract, such as a sales commission, are capitalized when the entity expects to recover them (340-40-25-1, 25-2). They may be expensed as incurred when the asset's amortization period would be one year or less (25-4, a practical expedient). The amortization period follows the transfer of the related goods or services and may include specific anticipated contracts such as renewals (35-1).` | FASB ASU 2014-09 Section A | Research note 2026-09-26-saas-ai-metrics.md `F5. Capitalized commissions are an asset` | FASB US GAAP taxonomy 2024, 2025 and 2026 (siglia-xbrl-element --offline, read 26 Sep 2026) `CapitalizedContractCostNet: cost incurred to obtain or fulfill contract with customer` `CapitalizedContractCostAmortization: cost incurred to obtain or fulfill contract with customer`

reading.text: ASU 2025-06 removes the project stages of Subtopic 350-40. Capitalization starts when two conditions hold: (1) management has authorized and committed to funding the project; (2) it is probable that the project will be completed and the software will be used to perform the function intended (the probable-to-complete threshold). That judgement also weighs significant development uncertainty: novel or unproven features not yet resolved through coding and testing, and performance requirements still being set or revised. The Board expects capitalization of software delivered through a cloud computing arrangement (SaaS) could decrease. It is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after 15 December 2027 and the interim periods within them. Early adoption is permitted in a period whose statements are not yet issued, from the start of that annual period, and there are three transition methods (prospective, modified, retrospective). So capitalized development, R&D expense and free cash flow after capitalized software can shift at adoption.

If the registrant knows of events reasonably likely to cause a material change in the relationship between costs and revenues, 'the change in the relationship must be disclosed.'

rules.says: RPO disclosure (50-13), with optional exemptions: 50-14(a), contracts with an original expected duration of one year or less; 50-14(b), the right-to-invoice expedient; and 50-14A, (a) a sales-based or usage-based royalty for a licence of intellectual property and (b) variable consideration allocated entirely to a wholly unsatisfied performance obligation, or to a wholly unsatisfied distinct promise within a series (25-14(b)) that meets 32-40. 50-14B: the 50-14(b) and 50-14A exemptions never apply to fixed consideration; 50-14(a) is not barred. A guaranteed minimum in an arrangement whose usage part is exempt is still disclosed unless the contract itself falls under 50-14(a), and so is variable consideration estimated for a partially satisfied obligation or promise (BC24). A company using any exemption must say which and describe what it left out (50-15).

rules.says: Incremental costs of obtaining a contract, such as a sales commission, are capitalized when the company expects to recover them (340-40-25-1, 25-2); the test is recoverability, not contract length. They may be expensed as incurred when the asset's amortization period would be one year or less (25-4, a practical expedient), and a filer may tag that election on RevenuePracticalExpedientIncrementalCostOfObtainingContract (true or false). The asset is amortized as the related goods or services transfer, over a period that may include specific anticipated contracts such as renewals (35-1). Read in the ASU as issued: later technical corrections to the Codification are unchecked.

checks.says: A direction word (rose, fell, increased, narrowed ...) with one period's figure ('to $X') and no comparison beside it: no 'from' figure, no change ('by 5%', 'up 5%', 'rose 19%', 'a 5% increase', '$8M more') and no figure after 'compared with', 'versus' or 'than'.
